label: first copy step after <DEL> in length-3 sequences
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase of the shortest sequences (L=3 accounts for 98.5% of activation mass). Its main firing point is step 4, the first step after <DEL>, where the input is the fed-back orig(0) and the model outputs orig(1). The top activations are all there, and they are strongest when orig(0) is p, q or 1. A weaker secondary firing at step 5 (the last output, recall_idx 2) accounts for about 10% of mass and is enriched when the input there is p/q/1/f/u/b. Adding that clause raises dev F1 from 0.84 to 0.89 but is token-specific, so it is left out. Rare weak activations occur in L=4 (1.5% of mass). Never fires in the original phase, on the <DEL> step, or for L>=5.

issues: Data scope: everything was scored on features/copy_gru_v1_neuron_baseline_store, not on the subsampled data you asked about. features/copy_transcoder_v2_1of5 holds only raw 1M_128_high_seq{3..9}.pt files and a subsample_manifest.json. There is no store there, so the autointerp tool can't run on it yet. A neuron-baseline store has to be built from that data before this baseline can be run on the subsample.

All the factual claims check out on the dev profile. L=3 holds 98.5% of the activation mass and L=4 holds 1.5%. Step 4 holds 89.7%, step 5 holds 10.1% and steps 6-7 hold about 0.2%. The unit never fires in the original phase, on the <DEL> step, or for L>=5. The top activations are all at step 4 with p, q or 1 as the input. The reported test scores reproduce exactly: P 0.953, R 0.744, F1 0.835, mass recall 0.898.

Systematic misses remain. 855 test steps that are active (10.2% of mass, about 26% of active steps) fall outside the predicate, and nearly all of them are L=3 step 5 (recall_idx==2). These are not scattered noise. The step-5 firing depends on the input token: (L==3)&(recall_idx==2)&in_tok in {p,q,1,f,u,b} has dev precision 0.78, while step 5 without the token condition has only 0.23. The token set is the same one that drives the strongest step-4 activations. So the unit looks like an L=3 copy-phase unit whose strength depends on the input token, with step 4 as its main mode.

The false positives (123 on test) are also token-dependent rather than random. At L=3 step 4 the unit stays silent when the input is a low-weight token such as w, i, 0, h or l. This matches the same per-token gain.

The label slightly overclaims. 'First copy step after <DEL> in length-3 sequences' implies the unit is exclusive to that step, but a consistent secondary mode at the final step (step 5) carries about 10% of mass. The explanation mentions this mode, but the label and predicate leave it out. Adding the token clause raises test F1 from 0.835 to 0.891 and mass recall from 0.898 to 0.968, so the clause is justified, not ad hoc.
skeptic.revised_label: length-3 copy phase: the first step after <DEL> (main mode), plus the final step when the input is p/q/1/f/u/b
skeptic.better_predicate: ((L == 3) & (recall_idx == 1)) | ((L == 3) & (recall_idx == 2) & isin(in_tok, [tok('p'), tok('q'), tok('1'), tok('f'), tok('u'), tok('b')]))
